newsitem.title: USA: Aerial to buy $75 million in PCS handsets.
newsitem.headline: Aerial to buy $75 million in PCS handsets.

text.p: Aerial Communications Inc said Tuesday it has agreed to buy a total of $75 million worth of Personal Communications Service, or PCS, handsets from Mitsubishi Wireless Communications Inc and Nokia Oy.
Earlier, Nokia said that its share of the contracts was worth about $40 million.
Mitsubishi Wireless is a joint venture between consumer electronics giant Mitsubishi Electric Corp and trading company Mitsubishi Corp.
Aerial said it will market Mitsubishi's G100 phone and Nokia's 2190 handset. Aeriel said the PCS units from both firms use plug-in subscriber identification module Smart Cards.

The Smart Card houses a microprocessor embedded on a plastic card to protect and store customer data. The Smart Card is inserted in the handset and makes it function for the caller, storing the data required for the particular "personal" features the customer has selected from Aerial.
